## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S2. This is audit backlog UX-10 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: /today (doctor), the queue display, the board.
Findings and reviewers: F-07, F-15 (order) · reviewers A-08, A-12.
Rationale: A 72-year-old escalated for fever and BP 168/96 was row 11 of 11 on the doctor's list, below the first screen, because rows sort by slot time and a walk-in holds a late nominal slot. The display listed A-05, B-02, A-06, A-09, A-07, A-08: patients holding A-07 watch A-09 go first.
Proposed UX behaviour: A clinic setting chooses the queue rule: token order, arrival order or appointment order (and whether booked patients go before walk-ins). Arrived patients sort by that rule on the doctor's day, on the board within a column and on the queue display, so the three always agree. Every row on the doctor's day shows the token. A nurse escalation is pinned above Next patient with its reason, in words. A walk-in is ordered by arrival, not by a far slot time. The display still shows tokens only, and names the doctor per token after a reassignment.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, doctor view, queue rail (audit note 3).
Components and tokens affected: Today list rows; Chip for Escalated. Setting in Settings → Clinical. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Back end: the ordering rule, the setting (audited), one ordered-queue query used by all three screens. Front end: Today, display, board.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code. The pilot clinic's queue rule must be known.
Clinical sign-off: Decision required before merge: question 10 of the validation plan (pilot doctor and receptionist), recorded on the issue.
Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: three screens and the live updates share the order.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) The queue rail inside the consultation (its own ticket). (2) Token slip printing (its own ticket). (3) Wait-time estimates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a nurse escalation, when the doctor opens the day at 1024 by 768, then the escalated visit is in the first viewport above Next patient with its reason in words
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the clinic's rule, when the display's Next list, the board column and the doctor's day are compared, then the order is the same
- [ ] **AC3.** Given arrived patients, when the doctor's day renders, then each row shows its token
- [ ] **AC4.** Given a walk-in who arrived at 09:58 with a nominal 19:00 slot, when the arrival rule is set, then she sorts by 09:58
- [ ] **AC5.** Given the ordered-queue query, when the escalation-first rule is removed, then the integration test fails; a change of the setting is audited and scoped to the tenant
- [ ] **AC6.** Given the queue display, when it is read, then it shows tokens and the doctor per token and no name
- [ ] **AC7.** Given English and Arabic, when axe runs on the doctor's day, then there is no violation and escalation is not conveyed by colour alone

## Test notes
